label: Approval policy
description: Who must approve a request before fulfillment starts. Stages run in order; the approvers of one stage decide in parallel, and the stage passes when all of them approve (mode all) or when the first one approves (mode any). A stage can be conditional, expire, and escalate. Catalog items name the policy their requests use.
usage: Keep policies short: one stage for routine items, a second stage only for higher risk (e.g. when variables.access_level == 'admin').
Prefer group or role approvers over a single person so approvals do not stall during absences; people can also delegate.
Give stages an expiry with escalation for time-sensitive requests.
constraints: id is unique; tenant policies start with tenant__.
entity must be a request entity with an approval binding.
1–10 stages with unique snake_case IDs; each has 1–20 approvers of kind group (group key), role (role ID) or field (record.<field> or variables.<question> holding a user or group).
mode is all or any; expiresAfterHours is 1–2160; onExpiry is reject or escalate, and escalate needs escalateTo and expiresAfterHours.
when is a CEL-subset boolean over record and variables.
The requester never approves their own request, and one person decides at most one step per stage.
Approvals in flight keep the policy they started with; changing stages is a permission change.

binding.description: Configuration object in a layer's spec catalog; not a layout node.

accessibility.keyboard: Not rendered directly; the approvals panel and the approvals inbox show its stages.

examples.description: Manager approval, then security for admin access
